questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate antonym of the underlined word.

Raw cut leather coats, and ruffles in all shapes and sizes provided a **__delicate__ **edge.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **crude**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"delicate"** means something that is very fine in texture or structure, easily broken or damaged; fragile. (नाज़ुक)

 
 
• **Example: **The **delicate **flowers were carefully arranged in the vase.
 
 
 
• **"Crude" **refers to something that is in a natural or raw state; not yet processed or refined. (अपरिष्कृत)
 
 
• **Example: **The** crude** oil needs to be refined before it can be used as fuel.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'delicate' **is **'crude'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **crude**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Petite **(छोटा): Small and slender; typically used to describe a woman's body.

 
 
• **Example:** She looked **petite **in her new dress.
 
 
 
• **Attractive **(आकर्षक): Pleasing or appealing to the senses.
 
 
• **Example: **The garden is very **attractive** with all the blooming flowers.
 
 
 
• **Laborious** (मेहनती): Requiring considerable effort and time.
 
 
• **Example:** The **laborious** task of cleaning the entire house took all day.

questions.question:
The sentence has been divided into three parts, identify the error segment in the sentence given below. Choose no error if there is no error in the sentence.

Her performance in the second round of the/ competition was even most impressive/ than her outstanding debut in the first round.

options.text: Her performance in the second round of the
than her outstanding debut in the first round.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the second part of the given sentence, the phrase 'even most impressive' is incorrect.
 
• The correct comparative phrase should be 'even more impressive'.
 
• Comparative adjectives are used to compare differences between the two objects they modify **(larger, smaller, faster, higher)**. They are used in sentences where two nouns are compared, in this pattern:** Noun (subject) + verb + comparative adjective + than + noun (object).**
 
• Therefore, the phrase 'even more impressive' should be used in place of 'even most impressive'.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct sentence: *Her performance in the second round of the competition was even** more impressive **than her outstanding debut in the first round*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Comparative adjectives are generally formed by adding the suffix "-er" to the adjective (e.g., taller, smarter, faster) or by using "more" before the adjective (e.g., more beautiful, more interesting, more impressive).
 
• When comparing more than two things, superlative adjectives are used, typically by adding the suffix "-est" (e.g., tallest, smartest, fastest) or by using "most" before the adjective (e.g., most beautiful, most interesting, most impressive).
